source: Gospel Question (Responses).xlsx — 128 anonymous responses collected 4–18 September 2026 (rows 2–129). The verbatim responses are kept out of the public repository; regenerate them with `node scripts/import-learner-questions.mjs <xlsx>` into data/private/.

families.label: Trials, suffering, and fairness
families.description: Why faithful people still struggle; loneliness in trials; why life seems easier for others; consequences of other people's choices.
observations: The largest family. Many learners assume obedience should prevent hardship and read trials as evidence that God is absent or displeased.
Some responses describe current pain or loneliness. Content must not imply that trials are punishments or that every trial has a knowable purpose.
Learning opportunity: Jesus Christ's own suffering and His promise to succor (Alma 7:11–12) reframe the question from 'why me?' to 'who is with me?'.

families.label: Knowing the gospel is true
families.description: Whether God and Jesus Christ are real, how to know the Restoration is true, building a testimony, and what to do when it doesn't feel certain.
observations: Many responses ask for proof. Elder Corbridge's distinction between primary and secondary questions, and his four methods of learning, fit this family directly.
Some responses suggest a feeling of pressure to believe. Content should invite honest inquiry, not demand conclusions.

families.label: Church history and hard questions
families.description: Imperfect leaders, changes in Church practice, critical media, and rumors.
observations: These are what Elder Corbridge calls secondary questions. The primary-questions investigation addresses how to approach them; individual historical topics need their own carefully sourced study (backlog).
Some responses repeat rumors or inaccurate claims; any future content should rely on official sources and avoid amplifying them.

families.label: Feeling and recognizing the Spirit
families.description: Not feeling the Spirit, spiritual highs and lows, telling one's own thoughts from inspiration, decisions, and spiritual gifts.
observations: Common misconception: the Spirit is always a strong emotion. Scripture describes many forms (peace, thoughts in the mind, a still small voice), and 3 Nephi 9:20 describes people who received the Spirit and 'knew it not'.
Genuine uncertainty: why spiritual experiences vary even when habits stay the same. Content should not promise a formula.

families.label: Repentance and repeated mistakes
families.description: How to repent, knowing when one is forgiven, and whether God still loves and forgives someone who keeps making the same mistake.
observations: Learners fear that repeated sin exhausts God's patience or makes repentance meaningless. Mosiah 26:30 and Moroni 6:8 speak directly to this.
Misconception: that existing imperfectly is itself sin. The difference between weakness and sin is a key learning opportunity (Ether 12:27).

families.label: Worthiness and being 'good enough'
families.description: Whether one is worthy, what it takes to reach the celestial kingdom, and comparing standards with others.
observations: Closely tied to repentance; addressed as a side question in again-and-again. A strong candidate for a dedicated future investigation on grace.

families.label: How the Atonement can be personal
families.description: How Jesus Christ could suffer for billions of people individually, and how God can know everyone personally.
observations: Only two responses, but the question goes to the heart of the gospel and connects to many other families (trials, repentance).
Scripture affirms that He knows each person (Alma 7:11–12; 3 Nephi 17) without explaining the mechanism. Content must keep that line clear.

families.label: Jesus Christ and the Godhead
families.description: Why Jesus Christ is the center of the gospel, how the Father and the Son relate to us, and the Savior's premortal role.
observations: Some ask whether the Father's love and the Son's love differ. John 3:16 and John 17 present them as united in purpose.
The premortal Council is a gentle future side question.

families.label: Fearing God and friendship with God
families.description: How scripture can command us to fear God while Jesus calls His disciples friends.
observations: A single response, chosen because it is an excellent vocabulary investigation: the scriptural sense of 'fear' (reverence and awe) versus terror (1 John 4:18; Guide to the Scriptures, 'Fear').

families.label: Families and loved ones after death
families.description: Whether family relationships continue, and what happens to loved ones who weren't members of the Church.
observations: Deeply personal: these questions are often about family members and friends of other faiths.
Scripture teaches that the gospel is preached to the dead and that God judges by the desires of the heart (D&C 137:7–9; D&C 138). Specifics about any individual's future must be left to God.

families.label: Eternity, judgment, and exaltation
families.description: What eternity will be like, the Millennium and Final Judgment, and becoming like Heavenly Father.
observations: Backlog. Pairs well with families-beyond-the-veil.

families.label: Prayer and answers
families.description: Whether God hears prayers and why answers aren't always clear.
observations: Strong candidate for the next release. Overlaps the 1.x question-bank entry 'meaningful-prayer' and the recognizing-the-spirit investigation.

families.label: Missions, patriarchal blessings, and readiness
families.description: Whether and when to serve a mission, and when and how to receive and understand a patriarchal blessing.
observations: Mostly personal-decision questions. A future investigation could study how scripture describes seeking guidance for decisions (D&C 9:7–9) rather than giving advice.

families.label: The Second Coming
families.description: Why the Second Coming isn't discussed more, why it is preceded by hard signs, and worry that it will come before one has a future.
observations: Some of these questions carry anxiety. A future study could pair the signs of the times with the Savior's counsel against fear (D&C 38:30; JS—Matthew).

families.label: Creation, science, and other worlds
families.description: Other worlds and life, the size and age of the universe, dinosaurs, and how science fits with the Creation.
observations: Large and curious family. Moses 1:33–39 and D&C 76:24 address worlds without number; many specifics are genuinely unrevealed and must be presented as such.

families.label: Commandments and Church practices
families.description: Fasting, the Word of Wisdom, the Sabbath, temple attendance, and meeting schedules.
observations: Backlog. The 1.x question bank already covers the Sabbath.

families.label: Women, priesthood, and sealing
families.description: Women's roles and priesthood, and sealing practices.
observations: Sensitive topics with official statements and ongoing teaching. Any future content needs careful sourcing and the project owner's review.

families.label: Sharing the gospel and ministering
families.description: Sharing the gospel naturally, helping friends and family, and Christlike friendship.
observations: Backlog. Christlike friendship connects to the Character of Christ Builder (charity, compassion).

families.label: Imperfect people and criticism
families.description: Unkindness among believers, self-righteousness, and criticism of the Church.
observations: Backlog. Connects to charity and meekness in the Character of Christ Builder.

families.label: Scripture study and connecting with the Savior
families.description: Building a scripture-study habit, a structured way to study Jesus Christ, and connecting with Him beyond routine answers.
observations: Requests for a structured, personal way to study the Savior shaped Connect with Christ and the Character of Christ Builder.

families.label: Temptation and relationships
families.description: Resisting temptation and navigating relationships.
observations: Personal; better served by trusted adults and leaders than by app content. Not planned as investigations.

families.label: Scripture curiosities
families.description: Specific people and events in the scriptures.
observations: Good Scripture Explorer candidates (Alma 63; Matthew 4:1–11).

families.label: Life direction and unclear responses
families.description: School, the future, personal plans, and responses that aren't questions.
observations: Not suitable for investigations.
